newsitem.title: CANADA: U.S. lost ability to restrict Canada grain flow.
newsitem.headline: U.S. lost ability to restrict Canada grain flow.

text.p: The United States lost its ability to restrict the flow of Canadian grain into the United States with the implementation of World Trade Organization rules after a cap on Canadian wheat imports expired Sept 12, 1995, an Agriculture Canada official said.

"There was some ability to restrict the flow of grain but they lost that under the implementation of the WTO and they don't have the power to have restrictions now," Canada Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale's spokesman Vern Greenshields told Reuters.

Canada agreed to restrict wheat exports to the United States to 1.5 million tonnes over a one-year period that ended Sept 12, 1995. Trade action threatened by the U.S. at that time was no longer allowed under WTO rules after that date.
"The flow of grain is significantly below what it had been under the expired, and I emphasize, expired, wheat cap," Greenshields said.
Neither the U.S. Trade Representative's office nor the U.S. Department of Agriculture has requested a meeting with Goodale or Agriculture Canada officials, he added.
"I'm not sure what they're concerned about," he said.
The U.S. trade and agriculture officials early Tuesday said they planned to request meetings with Canada to discuss potential grain problems before imports from Canada reach disruptive levels.
"Requests of meetings are fine but we don't have at the moment any requests, nor are there any plans to be meeting with the Americans," Greenshields said.
Canadian Wheat Board chief commissioner Lorne Hehn declined comment on the U.S. announcement.
The CWB on Thursday forecast Prairie production of wheat, barley, canola, flax, rye and oats to reach an all-time record high of 52.8 million tonnes.
The forecast led to some speculation that the CWB would be an agressive seller of wheat to U.S. millers.
